inputs.sbc_source: SEC XBRL AllocatedShareBasedCompensationExpense FY2025 (10-K) = $385M. Tax withheld on net-share settlement is not separately tagged; no combined figure published, so the add-back alone is used (understates the SBC charge slightly).
inputs.buyback_note: FY2023 $992M, FY2024 $999M, FY2025 $400M, H1-2026 $1,971M (PaymentsForRepurchaseOfCommonStock). CEG is a genuine repurchaser, so the flat share count is funded, not a convention.
inputs.projected_shares_note: Flat at 355.3M: SBC is expensed in the flows. The 50M Calpine consideration shares are already inside this count (non-SBC issuance, happened at close, so no forward dilution is modelled).
inputs.share_count_basis: fully diluted: 354.31M shares on the 10-Q cover at 2026-07-31 (EntityCommonStockSharesOutstanding) + ~1M incremental dilutive awards (IncrementalCommonSharesAttributableToShareBasedPaymentArrangements FY2025). Held FLAT because SBC is fully expensed.
inputs.fy0: FY2026E (pro-forma combined with Calpine; guidance year)
inputs.wacc_rationale: 8.5% USD, identical in every scenario (risk charged once, in the flows). Cost of equity ~10% (UST 10y ~4.3% + beta ~1.1 x 5.0% ERP); after-tax cost of debt ~4.5% (IG-rated, ~$1.07B annualised interest on ~$24.7B); weights ~83/17 equity/debt at market. Nuclear baseload under 20-year hyperscaler PPAs is lower-risk than the beta implies, the Calpine gas/retail book is higher, so no adjustment either way.
inputs.lease_treatment: US GAAP: operating lease cost already sits in O&M inside EBITDA; lease liabilities are NOT in net debt. One treatment, no double charge.
inputs.nci_treatment: Flows are consolidated; the $345M noncontrolling interest (2026-06-30, MinorityInterest) is deducted once in the equity bridge. NCI earnings are immaterial (FY2025 $4M).
inputs.net_debt_note: Total debt $24,700M at 2026-06-30 = LongTermDebtNoncurrent 19,111 + LongTermDebtCurrent 363 + ShortTermBorrowings 5,226 (the Metrics.csv TotalDebt of 19,474 omits short-term borrowings, which include the on-balance-sheet receivables facility that replaced the DPP sale in 2025 and acquisition-bridge borrowings). Cash $697M. Net debt $24,003M. The nuclear decommissioning trusts ($20.6B) are treated as funding their own ARO: neither the trust assets nor their gains (booked below operating income) enter the valuation.
inputs.notes: MODEL: owner-FCF DCF, component build, 10-year horizon (routing table: operating company, cyclical; owner-fcf.md + adaptations (f) risk-once and (c) NCI). CEG is a competitive/merchant generator and retail supplier, not a rate-base utility: there is no allowed return on a regulated asset base, so a utility RAB model does not apply. FCF BASIS: reported OCF is unusable as a base. FY2022-FY2024 OCF was structurally negative (-2,353 / -5,301 / -2,464) because collections on the deferred-purchase-price receivable sold to banks were classified in INVESTING (4,964 / 7,340 / 10,217); the DPP arrangement ended in 2025, so FY2025 OCF (4,237) is the first clean year, and collateral postings swing it by billions. Owner FCF is therefore built from components: pro-forma FY2026 EBITDA ~$9.25B derived from raised adjusted operating EPS guidance ($11.50-12.50 x ~357M diluted shares = ~$4.3B) + tax + ~$1.07B annualised interest + depreciation (~$1.75B annualised from H1-2026 $870M) + nuclear fuel amortization (~$1.0B; H1 $496M). Nuclear fuel is treated consistently: its amortization is added back inside EBITDA/D&A and fuel purchases sit inside capex (PaymentsToAcquirePropertyPlantAndEquipment includes nuclear fuel). FY0 = FY2026E pro-forma; revenue $37.0B = H1-2026 $18,626M grossed up by FY2025's H1 share (50.5%). Year 1 of the explicit build is FY2027. H2-2026 cash generation is neither in the flows nor in the June-2026 net debt, so an estimate is added in the equity bridge. last_fcf 903 = FY2025 standalone reported FCF 1,288 - SBC 385 (pre-Calpine, context only; not the projection base). DIVESTITURES: DOJ/FERC-mandated sales (Brazos Valley $860M to LS Power announced Aug-2026; five PJM assets, one ERCOT asset, Gregory stake) are treated as value-neutral (proceeds ~ PV of the flows given up) and not added to the bridge. Interest income: company is net-debt, nothing stripped. Pension/OPEB deficit not in the bridge (not quantified in the data available; a modest overstatement).

equity_bridge.item: H2-2026 owner FCF (FY0 is the guidance year; flows start FY2027)
equity_bridge.note: ~half of the FY2026E pro-forma owner FCF (~$2.9B = EBITDA 9.25B - SBC 0.44B - cash tax ~0.9B - capex ~5.0B); cash that lands on the balance sheet between the June balance sheet and year 1

historical_growth.growth_rate_source: judgment: base revenue path years 1-5 (~4-5%). Equity CAGR is unusable (Exelon spin-off separation FY2021-22, then $17.5B of stock issued for Calpine in Q1-2026); revenue 5yr CAGR is inflated by the 2021-22 power-price spike; EPS was negative in FY2021-22.
historical_growth.growth_divergence_warning: Equity 5yr CAGR 0.24% vs revenue 5yr 7.72% and EPS 2yr 21.4%: >30% divergence. Equity path is distorted by the spin-off and the Calpine share issuance, not by economics.

owner_fcf_history.basis: (OCF + DPP collections classified in investing) - capex - SBC; no meaningful CAGR (sign change, collateral swings)

historical_growth.notes: FCF CAGRs set null: owner FCF changes sign and is dominated by collateral and DPP classification, not by the business. Revenue is commodity-pass-through heavy, so margin, not revenue, carries most of the earnings growth (capacity prices, PPAs, Crane restart).

base.rationale: FY2026E pro-forma EBITDA margin ~25%; +3pp by FY2030 from PJM capacity at the ~$325/MW-day cap through 2029/30, Crane (835 MW, Microsoft PPA) back in service late 2027, ~1 GW of uprates and data-center PPA premia; held flat after. Capex ~13.5% in FY2026 (H1 $2.5B incl. nuclear fuel, Crane, uprates) fading to maintenance + fuel ~8.5%. Cash tax ramps from ~10-13% (FY2024-25 paid/pretax, credit purchases, bonus depreciation) to ~23% federal+state. Working capital negative capture: retail and wholesale receivables grow with revenue.

scenario_narratives.base: Calpine integrates without incident and the mandated divestitures clear near fair value. PJM capacity clears at or near the ~$325/MW-day collar through the 2029/30 delivery year, Crane returns to service in late 2027 under the 20-year Microsoft PPA, and the >5.6 GW data-center/clean-energy contract pipeline converts at a steady pace. Margin expands ~3pp to ~28% by FY2030 and then holds; capex fades from a restart/uprate peak to maintenance plus fuel. Earnings grow well, but slower than management's 20%+ EPS CAGR, which also leans on buybacks.
scenario_narratives.bull: AI load growth keeps PJM and ERCOT tight after the collar expires, so capacity and energy prices stay high; more hyperscaler deals are signed at premium, long-dated prices for nuclear baseload and Calpine's firm gas, and the uprate programme is extended. Margin reaches ~32% and revenue compounds 6-7% early, broadly consistent with management's 20%+ EPS growth ambition.
scenario_narratives.bear: Hyperscaler capex slows and data-center PPAs stall, the post-collar PJM market redesign or new supply pushes capacity prices toward the ~$175 floor, gas-fired spark spreads compress on the enlarged Calpine fleet, and integration and divestiture execution slip. Crane is delayed by the NRC. Margin drifts back to ~22%, below the pro-forma starting point, with ~2% revenue growth; leverage (~2.6x net debt/EBITDA) limits buybacks.

probability_weighted.weights_rationale: Bear raised to 20% from the 15% default: leverage roughly tripled with Calpine, integration and mandated divestitures are live, and capacity revenue depends on a single regulator's (FERC/PJM) market design. Base 50%: the collar and contracted PPAs give good visibility to 2029/30. Bull trimmed to 30%: it needs AI load growth, post-collar pricing and further PPA wins to all go right together.

valuation_philosophy.summary: A merchant/contracted power generator valued on owner FCF built from components off FY2026 guidance, because reported cash flow is distorted by receivable-sale classification and collateral. The market price sits well above the house base case: it is paying for margin expansion close to the bull path (AI-driven load growth persisting beyond the PJM collar).
key_risks_to_valuation: Capacity-price regime after the 2029/30 collar: each 1pp of terminal EBITDA margin is worth roughly $15-20/share
EBITDA base is derived from adjusted-EPS guidance, not a disclosed EBITDA figure; a 5% error in FY0 EBITDA moves value ~8-10%
Divestiture proceeds assumed value-neutral; the $5.2B of short-term borrowings is counted as debt
Cash-tax ramp: CEG has paid ~10-13% of pretax in FY2024-25; a slower ramp to 23% adds value
Terminal value capped at 15x FCF; nuclear licence extensions to 80 years support a long life, but the gas fleet and merchant exposure argue against a higher multiple
